---
title: "Joining relational data"
subtitle: "What happens to one row when we combine tables?"
---

This site collects the materials for the STAT 386 lesson on joining relational
data with pandas: the slide deck, slide-aligned follow-along code, a
15-minute pair activity with solutions, teaching notes, and the fictional
datasets that support them.

## Setup and use

Open this folder in Positron and run `uv sync`. Select the project Python
environment. Run cells in [follow_along.py](follow_along.py) at the matching
slide headings; each cell names its slide number. To run everything, use:

```bash
uv run python follow_along.py
```

The slide deck includes the complete output for each follow-along display,
with indexes omitted and missing values labeled NA.
[follow_along.ipynb](follow_along.ipynb) contains the same examples with
captured output. [explore_joins.py](explore_joins.py) adds deeper examples.

## Materials

| Material | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Slides](slides.qmd) | Lecture deck with Venn diagrams and worked join examples |
| [Pair activity](activity.qmd) | Instructions and data dictionary for the 15-minute pair activity |
| [Teaching notes](teaching-notes.qmd) | Timing, answers, and discussion guidance |
| [student_activity.ipynb](student_activity.ipynb) | Activity starter notebook |
| [activity_solutions.py](activity_solutions.py), [activity_solutions.ipynb](activity_solutions.ipynb) | Solutions; attempt the activity before opening them |
| `data/` | Seven fictional datasets |
| `assets/` | Editable SVG Venn diagrams |

The data dictionary on the [activity page](activity.qmd) defines the
`record_status` rule used in the activity repair.

## Editing the deck

The deck source is [slides.qmd](slides.qmd) with [lecture.css](lecture.css).
Static code listings and output tables require no Python execution to render;
update outputs when you edit code or data. The deck has 32 core slides and
three optional reference slides.

Venn circles represent distinct join keys and shading shows retained keys.
Matching pairs determine output row counts. All names, groups, measurements,
and conferences are fictional teaching data.

## Building the site

With Quarto installed, run `quarto render`. The site HTML is written to
`docs/`, ready to publish (for example, from GitHub Pages serving the `docs`
folder of the repository).
